title: Day 17 — LRU Cache with TTL
prompt: This LRU cache with TTL has two bugs: it evicts keys we just read, and it serves expired data. Time is injected as `now`. How would you fix the read path?

clarifications.answer: A get() on a present, non-expired key counts as a use — it becomes most-recently-used.
TTL is measured from INSERT time. A read does NOT reset the TTL — recency and expiry are two different clocks.
An entry expires when now - inserted > ttl. Exactly ttl later is still valid.
An expired entry should be removed when accessed (so size drops).
put and capacity-based eviction are already correct — the bugs are only in get.
now is passed in to get/put, so tests are deterministic — no real clock in the logic.

hints: Two separate concerns: LRU order (recency) and TTL (expiry from insert). A read touches recency but not TTL.
In get: if now - inserted > ttl, delete the key and return None; otherwise move_to_end(key) and return the value.
The starter get() does neither move_to_end nor the ttl check — add both, in that order.
